newsitem.title: USA: Calif. exports of manufactured goods top $100 bln.
newsitem.headline: Calif. exports of manufactured goods top $100 bln.

text.p: California exports of manufactured goods topped $104 billion in 1996, up 8.16 percent from 1995, state trade officials said on Thursday.
The California Trade and Commerce Agency said exports in 1996 broke the $100 billion mark for the first time in the state's history.
The agency said Japan and Canada were California's two largest export markets. Mexico boosted its position, surpassing Korea to become California's third largest export market, the agency said.

"International trade accounts for a quarter of the state's trillion-dollar gross state product," said Trade and Commerce Agency Secretary Julie Meir Wright. "As is evidenced by these preliminary numbers, exports are becoming a pillar in California's new economy."
California's leading export sectors continued to be electronics and electronic equipment, industrial machinery, specialized instruments, transportation equipment and agricultural products.
The agency said service exports from California account for an additional $40 billion a year.
